Meanwhile, U.S. equity futures were little changed, with Nasdaq flat, S&P 500 up 0.05%, and Dow futures up 0.07%.
In commodity markets, crude oil slipped toward $89 per barrel, while gold fell below $4,350 an ounce. Digital assets maintained key levels.

South Korea’s KOSPI rose 0.46% to approximately 7,050, advancing for a fourth straight session as the South Korean won strengthened to around 1,351 per dollar. Market sentiment was supported by the Asian Development Bank raising South Korea's 2026 growth forecast to 3.2% from 2.6%, citing robust export demand, solid corporate earnings, and expansionary fiscal policy, despite ongoing risks from global trade tensions and financial volatility.

The offshore yuan weakened to around 6.70 per dollar ahead of Xi’s first U.S. visit since 2015. Chinese President Xi Jinping and First Lady Peng Liyuan are scheduled to be welcomed by President Trump on Wednesday evening, marking Xi's first visit to the United States since 2015.
